messages:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT P-2187 triggered: high 5xx rate on hosted inference in us-west-2. alerting on service=redwood-serving-runtime, symptom=CUDA OOM spikes and container restarts. auto-page Maya (oncall) and infra-ops.
Maya (oncall): seeing ~18% 5xx on /v1/generate, brief spike 2m ago then sustained. GPU OOM stderr in pods: `tensorflow/runtime/cuda: out of memory` and `Segmentation fault (core dumped)` in runtime sidecar. Paging now.
Sanjay: can confirm logs from 3 replicas show repeated OOMs at allocation ~6.7GB then crashloop. Likely memory pressure from an autoscale rapid-up event — pods started with heavier batch configs.
Leah: any recent rollout? I didn't see model changes in last 6h. Rolling window shows 2x scale-up in 90s. Autoscaler logs show many add/remove decisions: `scale delta +12 -> -10 -> +8` (thrash).
Jonah: putting incident to P1 given customer impact and error rate. Which customers affected? Marta, any telemetry?
Marta: SRE dashboards show elevated 5xx for routes serving enterprise customers: acct-87 and acct-142. Error type: 503 when runtime exits, increased latency for all others. Not widespread yet but trending.
Maya (oncall): immediate actions: 1) Pause autoscaler (set mode=manual) to stop churn. 2) Set serving-runtime to fallback model variant that is lower memory. 3) Increase pod restart backoff / cooldown. Who can flip autoscaler?
infra-ops: on it. Running `kubectl annotate hpa autoscaler-serving redwood/paused=true` and patching cluster-autoscaler scale-down-delay to 10m. Executing now.
Sanjay: while autoscaler paused, recommend cordon recently added nodes that show repeated node flaps: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-7 gpu-node-9` to avoid noisy hardware. Also taint them `maintenance=true:NoSchedule`.
Leah: applying model fallback: updating routing policy to pin to `mistral-7b-qa` (lower kv cache) for affected routes. Patch command: `curl -X POST /admin/routing -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"mistral-7b-qa","reason":"OOM mitigation"}'`
Marta: told sales/SRE for acct-87 and acct-142 that we're mitigating, ETA 10-15m. Customer-facing note prepared: "Experiencing intermittent errors; currently mitigating; we will provide update in 30m."
Jonah: also let's scale down batch sizes to aggressive single-token policy to limit memory transient spikes. Maya, can you flip config?
Maya (oncall): changing batch policy now: `cfg.set('batch.max_tokens', 64); cfg.set('batch.max_requests', 1)` pushing.
infra-ops: autoscaler paused, scale-down-delay increased, cordoned two nodes. Observed crashloop frequency dropped but OOMs continue on a subset.
Sanjay: spotted kernel log on gpu-node-9: `NVRM: Xid (Error) 13, PID 14234` repeated, suggests GPU driver errors correlated with OOM. I'll open node-level driver restart if needed.
Leah: can we drain the flapping nodes gracefully? Want to avoid additional evictions.
infra-ops: `kubectl drain gpu-node-9 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120` in progress.
Jonah: set incident comms: severity=Sev2 -> bump to Sev1 if customer impact widens. Update pagerduty.
Marta: added an incident status message to workspace and notified account teams.
Sanjay: quick check: runtime config had experimental continuous-batching enabled for hotpath — rolling that back now. Patch: `kubectl set env ds/serving-runtime CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=false` deploy rolling.
Maya (oncall): runtime pods are restarting with new env, slight dip in OOMs. Autoscaler still paused.
infra-ops: GPU driver restart scheduled on drained node; if driver recovers we'll uncordon. Running `systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced` and reloading driver.
Sanjay: after driver restart I see one node stable, tests for allocation succeed. But autoscaler must be tuned — current oscillation is the upstream cause.
Leah: plan for short-term: keep autoscaler paused for 20m, keep fallback model for affected routes, continue cordoning suspect nodes, and monitor error rate. Long-term: adjust autoscaler hysteresis and bump cool-down to 5m, implement rate-limited ramp-up and model-aware scaling.
Jonah: agreed. Also add temporary quota to limit concurrent requests per account to protect noisy tenants. Marta, coordinate comms.
Marta: quota applied for acct-87 and acct-142: `concurrency: 6` for now. Customer teams notified.
Maya (oncall): handing off to Sanjay for overnight mitigation and follow-up. @Sanjay you are primary, @Leah secondary. I'm logging details into the incident tracker.
Sanjay: taking handoff. Notes: root cause hypothesis — autoscaler feedback loop + transient GPU driver/device memory fragmentation causing OOMs under aggressive batch/ramp-up. Immediate remediation steps performed: autoscaler paused, reduced batch sizes, model fallback, cordoned/drained suspect nodes, driver restart. Next: playbook actions to tune autoscaler policy, add model-compatibility tags to routing so autoscaler avoids ramping heavy models, and postmortem.
infra-ops: leaving a small watch: `kubectl get pods -n serving -w` and `kubectl describe node gpu-node-*` in tmux.
Maya (oncall): officially closing pager duty escalation for me, assigning P-2187 to Sanjay. Leaving Slack thread to oncall.
Sanjay: I'll continue monitoring for 2h and assemble a mitigation PR for autoscaler config: `autoscaler.cooldownSeconds=300`, `minScaleStabilization=120`.
Leah: capturing config diffs in a PR draft and will include load-test plan to validate hysteresis.
Marta: scheduling customer follow-up mention in 60m with updated ETA.
Jonah: adding postmortem owner tag: Sanjay. Please include timelines, mitigations, and action items.
Sanjay: ACK, adding timeline and logs.
infra-ops: final status 30m after initial page: 5xx down to ~1.2%, affected routes stable under fallback. Will uncordon nodes one-by-one after further validation. :white_check_mark:
Maya (oncall): thanks team — great quick coordination.
pagerduty-bot: P-2187 transitioned to "acknowledged" and reassigned to Sanjay.
